_about: Shock fields: the lethal ring of chapter 3, decoded from android_game.bin
(ETHCallback_shock_agent and ETHCallback_shock_area, which share one source file).
TWO entities in the original, ONE here. A placed shock_agent is a one-shot builder: on
its first frame it spawns a separate shock_area.ent at its own position with z -10,
sizes it to the diameter with scaleToSize, and writes currentScale, squaredRadius,
ownerID, speed, stride and direction onto it, then sets areaAdded so it never builds
again. The AREA carries the lethal radius; the AGENT is the sprite. Both then oscillate
with the same speed and stride and both seed their angle at 0, so the port models one
moving point. The area is created at instruction 54 of the agent's first frame and the
agent's own linearMotion runs at instruction 287 of that same frame, so the area
captures its originalPos BEFORE the agent has moved: both centres are the node's
position, and the only divergence is one frame of phase - about 0.03 rad at level27b's
1.8 rad/s, which is 0.03 px on a 64 px stride.
THE PLACED NODE IS THE CENTRE OF THE OSCILLATION, NOT THE STARTING POSITION. angle
seeds at 0 and the offset is cos(angle) * stride * sign(speed), so cos(0) = 1 puts the
ring a full stride from the node on its very first frame. A port that treated the node
as the start would misplace level27b's ring by 64 px, and the suite asserts the
displacement rather than only the radius so that either model cannot pass.
ONE range, and it is areaRadius. The kill is squaredDistance(player, area) <
squaredRadius where squaredRadius = scale(areaRadius)^2, then SetInt('hp', 0). It is a
poll EVERY frame, not an entry test - unlike a hazard, which fires on body_entered - so
a player that is inside dies whether it walked in or was put there.
THE CONVERTER'S COLLIDER IS NOT THE RING. Every shock_agent node carries a Body
(Area2D) with a CollisionShape2D of a CircleShape2D whose radius is 30 - the same 30 in
every level, against areaRadius values of 28 to 105. It is sprite-sized geometry and
has nothing to do with the lethal radius. LevelBuilder gives it isTrigger, so it is a
sensor the player passes through and not a platform; the port moves that entity with
the field so the sensor and the sprite follow the ring, and reads the radius from
areaRadius alone.

_note: Not tuning - the original has no global here, every number is per placement. This is
the validation floor, kept for the reason every other LoadRules keeps one: a radius
of nothing is a ring that kills nothing, and it would look like a level that works.
Find also refuses a placement whose speed and stride disagree about whether it moves,
since a speed with no stride is motion that never goes anywhere and a stride with no
speed is an amplitude nothing drives.
lazily on its first call, then each frame angle += unitsPerSecond(speed) - so speed is
RADIANS PER SECOND - wrapping by subtracting 2*PI once it passes it. The displacement
is cos(angle) * stride * sign(speed) along one axis, rotated by a matrix built from a
startAngle argument which both call sites pass as 0.
direction IS COPIED AND NEVER READ. The agent reads metadata/direction with GetString
and SetStrings it onto the area, and then neither callback consults it: both call
linearMotion with a hardcoded vertical flag. So the port moves vertically always. Both
placements that carry the key say 'vertical' anyway, so nothing in the game
distinguishes the two readings - which is why this is recorded rather than guessed at.
Only 2 of the 21 placements move at all: level14c (speed 2, stride 32) and level27b
(speed 1.8, stride 64). level14c is in chapter 4 and does not start, so exactly one
moving ring is reachable in the game as the port plays it today.

_census: 21 placements across 16 levels, areaRadius from 28 to 105.
In the 7 levels that start: level23b 80 and 60, level24b 60, level25b 105, level26b 74,

_not_built: Presentation, in a renderer-free port: the area spins at AddToAngle(unitsPerSecond(20)),
throbs by a random factor between 0.993 and 1.007 of its scale every frame, is tinted
(0.8, 1, 1) * 0.5, and sits at z -10 behind its agent. The agent calls bounce(0.95,
0.95, 300) - which is the blinkElapsedTime pulse of utilEntityEffect, not physics, as
the shock diamond's is. With them playShockStrikeSound and the shock_death.ent spawned
on the body when the ring kills.
BURNABLE, and it is already consistent. 11 of the 21 placements carry metadata/burnable,
of which only level30b's is in a level that starts. Fire::Find is flag-filtered, so that
agent IS in Fire's burnables list and does get `burned` set when lit - but removal is
gated on fade_names, which holds only the crate spellings, so Fire never takes it away.
fire.json's burn._note already says so in as many words. Nothing here needs wiring, and
no ring can outlive its agent.
The agent's destroy path is therefore unreachable too: isDestroyed leads to
shock_death.ent, small_explosion.ent, deleteEntity(childID) - which takes the ring with
it - and DeleteEntity(self). What would set `destroy` is a blast, whose filter is
isBreakableOrExplosiveOrBurnable and so does include a burnable agent; but fire.json
already records the blast's `destroy` as not built, for the reason that one body with
